wayback._note: The archive layer is written by scratch/pull-archive-tcv.py, not by wayback-pull.py eras: tcv.com carried a company list in almost every year since 2000 across seven site generations whose markups differ (a 2000-2002 alphabetical table, 2002-2006 sector pages, the 2007-2011 index.php4 dt/dd list, the 2011-2013 all-portfolio.php4 dd list, the 2013-2016 WordPress partnerships grid, the 2017-2026 compliance list /all-companies and the 2017-2023 /companies/ grid whose card classes carry the firm's own deal type (minority | majority | public), active flag, sector and deal partners, and the 2024-2026 Next.js /partnerships grid). The script reads the first and the last capture of each year per surface through scripts/ia_fetch.py and writes sources/wayback/parsed/<year>.json rows in the builder's shape, with name_listed keeping the archive's own rendering where the canonical name map (sources/site/name-map.json) maps it onto the live compliance list's company.

roster._note: Profile pages under /team/<first-last> (2019-2026) and /teams/<first-last> (2015-2016) are swept from the CDX by partner-roster.py; the 2002-2013 pages are /team/<first_last>.html (underscore, no hyphen) and are added by scratch/roster-old-pages.py with their capture years. The live team (sources/site/team.json) mixes investors with operations, finance and investor-relations staff: only the site's own role 'Investor' is kept as current-year roster evidence (site_team_groups). Tenure windows come from capture spans and from the natural persons on the firm's own fund Form Ds (the Thrive shape for the pre-2002 partners), one basis line per person in sources/wayback/roster-notes.json.

site_api._entry_stage_note: No TCV surface states an entry round: the compliance list is names only, the partnerships pages carry founding year, location, sector and the deal team, and the 2018-2023 grid's classes carry a deal TYPE (minority / majority / public), which is a control and T3 label, never a stage (stage_words.py knows no such word). Nothing is eligible to label entry_stage (COLLECTION.md 5); the firm's own news posts are class 1 for the round each one names and assert an entry only where they say so in words (COLLECTION.md 6).

sources._note: One row per company, merged by scratch/merge-site-tcv.py from the three live first-party surfaces: the compliance list tcv.com/all-companies (339 legal names, as of 2026-07-15), the partnerships grid and pages (155, with the deal team), and the Getro job board portfoliojobs.tcv.com (62). The join uses sources/site/name-map.json (curated: the grid's brand to the list's legal name). url is the partnership page where one exists, else the compliance list.

site_api._note: tcv.com is Next.js App Router over Contentful (space ue5a638q2a2b); every surface ships its data in the page's RSC flight payload, read without an API key (escalation ladder step 5). The job board is Getro (portfoliojobs.tcv.com); its stage field is never a label.

edgar._note: 'TCV' is distinctive on EDGAR once qualified: 108 registrants in the lookup table start TCV or Technology Crossover, all the firm's own funds, general partners, relying advisers and single-deal 'Co' vehicles, except three namesakes (TCV Trust & Wealth Management, Inc. of Richmond, a trust company that files its own 13F; TCVI Group Inc.; TCV Franchise Fund LP, checked by address) and the third-party access feeders (desks.classify). Each fund's general partner files its own 13F-HR (Technology Crossover Management IV LLC 2002-2013, V 2007-2019, VI 2009-2019, VII Ltd 2012-2023, VIII Ltd 2017-2026, IX Ltd 2018-2026, X Ltd 2021-2026, XI Ltd 2023-2026; thirteenf_ciks), so a 13F line names the fund holding a listed position. The funds file Schedule 13D/G and Forms 3/4 themselves: fund-filing evidence for a listed member. The adviser is TCMI, Inc. (CRD 160389) with relying advisers TCV VI, VII, VIII, IX Management and TCV Management 2004. Seed queries are URL-ready (edgar-entities.py does not encode them: 'technology crossover' with a space returned nothing).

desks._note: One adviser, one strategy (COLLECTION.md 1, T1; decisions.md D1-D2): TCMI, Inc. (CRD 160389) and its relying advisers advise all 34 private funds on the 2026-03-27 ADV, and their Section 7.B gross assets sum to the Item 5.F RAUM to the dollar ($22,506,060,259), so there is no second strategy family to partition: the public and private positions sit in the same growth funds (the PRO-169 delta), and T3 decides each row. External: the three namesakes above and the access feeders into TCV XI, XII and Global Growth XIII where their filing address is a third party's (the Thrive IX Access precedent; checked in the run). TCV Acquisition Corp., the firm's own blank-check company, sits on the home desk as a vehicle and is never a row (T5; a promote would be out under the sponsor-promote ruling), and it is a membership trap in verify.not_members.

profile._note: TCMI, Inc. (CRD 160389, SEC-registered, primary business name TCV) reports RAUM $22,506,060,259 on the 2026-03-27 annual amendment (sources/registers/adv-160389.json), 34 private funds whose Section 7.B gross assets sum to the RAUM exactly. There is no strategy partition, so the RAUM is the firm's AUM floor. focus_min_companies is about 4.5% of the expected base.

verify._unicorn_bands_note: Rule A (Erik 2026-09-06): the unicorn snapshot is an aggregator, a coverage floor to verify, never a mark.

shape._note: The $1B+ share has no ceiling (COLLECTION.md 8, Erik 2026-09-26): a growth and crossover book can sit at any share, so the share is stated in the report and not gated. c2a_rate_max restates the 80% default; the Seed cohort is expected to be thin or empty (PRO-169: no new stage, entries are Growth by design).

verify._not_members_note: Membership traps (COLLECTION.md 10 invariant 11), written 2026-09-29 before any verdict from decisions.md D4, D6, D8 and D9: TCV's own blank-check company, the acquirers whose stock the 13F shows arriving at a portfolio company's sale, and listed holdings from TCV I to III that the firm's compliance list excludes by its own note.
verify._known_positions_note: Positions the firm documents as its own private-round, minority investments: its posts and press releases (sources/site/news-archive.json), the funds' Schedule 13D/G filings, and the 2018-2023 grid's own 'minority' deal type. Verify fails if one is missing from the published base. Expedia was dropped before any verdict: the grid labels it a 'public' deal (decisions.md D6).
